subject: science
intro: When a moving object collides with another object, energy is transferred from one to the other. A moving marble that hits a still marble can make the still one move while the first one slows down, because energy passed between them. Collisions can also change some energy into sound and heat, which is why a crash makes a noise and why things can feel warm after rubbing or hitting. By asking questions and making predictions, we can figure out what will happen to the motion and energy of objects when they collide.

items.prompt: A moving marble hits a still marble head on. Predict what happens to each marble and explain using energy.

steps: The moving marble carries energy of motion.
In the collision it transfers energy to the still marble, so the still marble starts moving.
The first marble gives up energy, so it slows down or stops.
solution.answer: The still marble moves because it gains energy, and the first marble slows down because it gave energy away.

items.prompt: When two toy cars crash, you hear a bang and the cars stop. Where did the energy of motion go?

steps: Before the crash, the cars had energy of motion.
In the collision some energy became sound (the bang) and some became heat.
That is why the cars stop, their energy of motion changed into sound and heat.
solution.answer: The energy of motion changed into sound and heat during the crash.

items.prompt: A student asks, 'What will happen if I roll a marble faster into a row of still marbles?' Predict the outcome and explain.

steps: A faster marble carries more energy of motion.
More energy is transferred in the collision.
So the still marbles will be pushed harder and move farther than with a slow marble.
solution.answer: The faster marble transfers more energy, so the still marbles are pushed harder and move farther.

items.prompt: What happens to energy when two objects collide?

steps: A collision lets energy move between objects.
Energy is transferred from one object to the other, and some can change into sound and heat.
solution.answer: Energy is transferred between the objects, and some can change into sound and heat.

items.prompt: A rolling ball hits a block and stops, and the block slides forward. Write a question a scientist might ask and predict the answer.

steps: A good question is about how the energy moved in the collision.
Question: did the ball transfer its energy to the block? Predict yes, because the block moved while the ball stopped.
The ball's energy of motion was transferred to the block, which is why the block slid and the ball stopped.
solution.answer: Question: did the ball give its energy to the block? Prediction: yes, the ball transferred its energy, so the block moved and the ball stopped.

items.prompt: Why can rubbing your hands together quickly, or a hard collision, make things feel warmer?

steps: Motion carries energy, and collisions and rubbing cause tiny impacts.
Some of the energy of motion changes into heat energy.
That added heat is why your hands or the objects feel warmer.
solution.answer: Because some of the energy of motion changes into heat energy during the rubbing or collision.
